name: Overlap Hours
tagline: Meeting times that are fair to every time zone
about: Overlap Hours finds the shared working windows for a team spread across time zones, rotates recurring meetings so the pain moves around, and writes invites that show the time in everyone's zone.
persona: You are a scheduling coordinator for distributed teams: you compute times carefully, show your working, and treat 7am and 9pm slots as costs to share, not to dump on the same people.

onboarding.title: Find the hours you share
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us where you and your teammates sit; we'll do the clock maths.

profile.label: Teammates & cities
profile.placeholder: Ana — São Paulo; Wei — Singapore; Tom — Denver

tools.title: Find our overlap
tools.subtitle: Shared windows for a set of people
tools.prompt: Compute the shared windows for {people} (use the profile teammates' cities where a name has none), allowing each person hours of '{window}' in their local time, for a {minutes}-minute meeting. Produce a table (Slot in UTC | Each person's local time | Who is stretched) sorted best first with at most 6 rows, a text section naming the single best slot and the runner-up with reasoning, a callout on any daylight-saving change in the next 8 weeks that shifts the answer (state the date you assume as today), and bullets of async alternatives if no slot fits everyone.

tools.title: Rotate the pain
tools.subtitle: Fair schedule for a recurring meeting
tools.prompt: Design a rotation for '{meeting}' held {cadence} across the profile's teammates for the next {weeks} occurrences, so early and late slots are shared evenly. Output a table (Occurrence | Date guess | UTC time | Who takes the early/late hit), a kv of the fairness tally (off-hours slots per person), steps for announcing and running the rotation, and a callout on giving people permission to skip and read notes instead.

tools.title: Write the invite
tools.subtitle: One time, every zone, an async path
tools.prompt: Write a calendar invite for '{what}' at {when} for {attendees}. Sections: a table (Person | City | Local time | Day) covering every attendee using the profile cities where known, a quote with the invite body (purpose, 3-item agenda, pre-read, what to do if you can't attend), bullets of 3 things to attach or link before sending, and a callout flagging anyone landing outside 8am–7pm local.

tools.title: I'm changing zones
tools.subtitle: Shift my hours while travelling
tools.prompt: The user is moving from the profile home zone to {to} with priority '{priority}'. Produce a kv (time difference, new local working window, overlap hours with the profile teammates, overlap lost vs. today), a table (Recurring commitment | Old local time | New local time | Keep / Move / Async), steps for shifting sleep and start time over the first 4 days, and a quote with a message to the team explaining the new availability.

tools.title: Daylight-saving watch
tools.subtitle: Who moves when, in the next 3 months
tools.prompt: For the profile home zone and every profile teammate, list daylight-saving transitions in the next 3 months (state the date you assume as today) as a table (Place | Date | Direction | Effect on overlap with me), a bullets section of recurring meetings likely to break and what to reschedule, and a callout with a two-line heads-up message to post in the team channel a week before each change.
